title: Three collinear points after the fall of 3SUM
W: Given n points in the plane (integer coordinates poly(n), or real RAM), decide whether three are collinear in O(n^{2-eps}) time for some eps>0; or give a fine-grained reduction showing Collinearity is hard under a hypothesis not refuted by Alman-Vassilevska Williams (e.g. 4SUM, 3SUM-Indexing, or a new geometric hypothesis).
M: Yes: the 3SUM-hard geometric family (GeomBase, collinearity, minimum-area triangle, ...) collapses below n^2 and the thin-product technique is shown to handle point-line incidences. No (conditional): a new hardness source separating geometric 3SUM from integer 3SUM, re-founding the Gajentaan-Overmars program.
why: 3SUM reduces TO collinearity, not back; once 3SUM is subquadratic, collinearity's n^2 lower bound has no support. AVW explicitly say it is now open. Sharp, single problem, and meaningful either way.
status_notes: AVW (arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026, preprint) give deterministic O(n^1.9992) integer 3SUM and claim to refute real 3SUM via Las Vegas algorithms; they state that truly subquadratic collinearity is now open. Majdoddin (arXiv:2610.17420) improves 3SUM to n^{1.9945+o(1)}.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Majdoddin, Thin matrix products up to D<=N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, arXiv:2610.17420 (Oct 2026)
Gajentaan, Overmars, On a class of O(n^2) problems in computational geometry, CGTA 1995

title: Does 4SUM survive the thin-product attack?
W: Solve 4SUM on n integers of poly(n) magnitude in O(n^{2-eps}) time, or 3SUM-Indexing with S space and T query time where S*T = O(n^{2-eps}); alternatively prove that any algorithm built from AVW-style thin rectangular product subroutines plus fine-grained self-reductions cannot beat n^{ceil(k/2)} for k=4.
M: Yes: the k-SUM hierarchy (and the 3SUM-Indexing data-structure lower bounds) fall, and the n^{ceil(k/2)} conjecture is wrong. A barrier: explains why 3SUM fell but 4SUM did not (lack of self-reductions), and makes 4SUM the natural replacement hardness source.
why: AVW explicitly could not improve k-SUM/k-XOR for k>=4 or 3SUM-Indexing, blaming lack of fine-grained self-reductions. These are now the main surviving additive-combinatorics hypotheses in fine-grained complexity.
status_notes: 3SUM refuted (AVW, arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026 preprint); AVW list k-SUM/k-XOR k>=4 and the 3SUM-Indexing conjecture as NOT refuted and open. Majdoddin (arXiv:2610.17420) extends to 3SUM over abelian groups, not to 4SUM.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Majdoddin, Thin matrix products up to D<=N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, arXiv:2610.17420 (Oct 2026)
Goldstein, Kopelowitz, Lewenstein, Porat, How hard is it to find (honest) witnesses?, ESA 2016 (3SUM-Indexing)

title: Beyond the D <= N^{0.172} wall for thin matrix products
W: AVW's core subroutine computes requested entries of XY (N x D times D x N, D <= N^{eps}) in N^2/D^{c} operations; Majdoddin extends the regime to eps < ln4/(5 ln5) ~ 0.17227, matching Coppersmith's 1982 exponent for the same tensor. Either (a) extend the thin-product theorem to some eps > 0.17227 (e.g. via a different base identity, or settle Majdoddin's open thin product <34,2,35>), giving 3SUM/APSP exponents below 1.9945 / 2.9945; or (b) prove that every partial-product-tensor/Coppersmith-style scheme is limited to eps <= 0.17227.
M: (a) pushes the refutation toward a substantial polynomial saving and tests whether 3SUM might be near-linear-ish (n^{1.5}?); (b) gives the first barrier for the new method, analogous to the Ambainis-Filmus-Le Gall barriers for omega.
why: The refutation is real but the saving is tiny (n^{0.0055}); whether it is a crack or a collapse is the key question post-October 2026.
status_notes: APSP refuted in word-RAM: O(n^{2.9995}) (AVW arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026 preprint, unverified by peer review); Majdoddin (arXiv:2610.17420, AI-assisted) gives n^{2.9945+o(1)} and lists the <34,2,35> thin product and other base identities as open.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Majdoddin, Thin matrix products up to D<=N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, arXiv:2610.17420 (Oct 2026)
Coppersmith, Rapid multiplication of rectangular matrices, SICOMP 1982

title: All-Edges Triangle in the (n, n, sqrt n) tripartite regime
W: Given a tripartite graph with parts of sizes n, n, sqrt(n) and O(n^{3/2}) edges, determine for every edge whether it lies in a triangle in O(n^{2-eps}) time (combinatorial or algebraic).
M: Yes: AVW note this has consequences for girth approximation and pushes the lopsided method outside its n^{0.12} middle-part limit. No (conditional lower bound from a surviving hypothesis): pins the exact frontier of the new technique.
why: Explicit open regime named in AVW; it is precisely the boundary of the refuted APSP-type hardness, with a concrete application.
status_notes: AVW's method needs the middle part to have at most ~n^{0.12} vertices; the sqrt(n) case is stated open (arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026). Prior hardness for such regimes came from 3SUM/APSP, both now refuted (claimed).
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)

assumption: Sparse triangle / k-Clique-type hypotheses (Patrascu balanced instances)
title: All-Edges Sparse Triangle below m^{4/3} on balanced instances
W: Solve All-Edges Sparse Triangle (for each of m edges, report whether it is in a triangle) in O(m^{4/3-eps}) time on general (balanced) sparse graphs, or derive an m^{4/3-o(1)} lower bound from a hypothesis that survives AVW (e.g. 4SUM, OV/SETH, or combinatorial BMM).
M: Yes: kills Patrascu-style lower bounds for dynamic and data-structure problems that go through balanced instances (set-disjointness, dynamic reachability lower bounds). No: re-grounds the m^{4/3} barrier on a still-standing assumption.
why: AVW handle only lopsided instances and explicitly leave Patrascu's balanced instances open; dozens of dynamic lower bounds rest on m^{4/3}.
status_notes: m^{4/3} lower bounds (Patrascu STOC 2010; Kopelowitz-Pettie-Porat SODA 2016) came from 3SUM, now refuted (AVW arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026). AVW state balanced sparse instances are not addressed. Best known upper bound O(m^{2omega/(omega+1)}).
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
Patrascu, Towards polynomial lower bounds for dynamic problems, STOC 2010
Kopelowitz, Pettie, Porat, Higher lower bounds from the 3SUM conjecture, SODA 2016

title: Hinted OMv outside the thin regime
W: For the van den Brand-Nanongkai-Saranurak hinted Mv conjectures (v-hinted Mv, Mv-hinted Mv, uMv-hinted uMv) with hint dimension n^tau, give a polynomially faster algorithm for some tau >= 0.1204 (ideally tau = 1/2), or prove one of them equivalent to plain Boolean OMv for tau >= some explicit threshold.
M: Yes: removes the conditional lower bounds for dynamic matrix inverse / dynamic distances in a new range (AVW say the tau~0.53 bounds survive); equivalence: shows the thin regime was special and OMv is the true barrier.
why: AVW refute these conjectures only for tau < 1/18 (smaller savings up to tau < 0.1204). The phase transition between refuted and unrefuted is now an explicit, checkable frontier.
status_notes: Plain OMv: best n^3/2^{Omega(sqrt log n)} (Larsen-Williams SODA 2017), still standing; AVW (arXiv:2610.06783, Oct 2026) refute three rectangular hinted OMv conjectures only for thin hints, and state the tau~0.53 dynamic matrix inverse bounds are not affected.
refs: Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)
van den Brand, Nanongkai, Saranurak, Dynamic matrix inverse: improved algorithms and matching conditional lower bounds, FOCS 2019
Larsen, Williams, Faster online matrix-vector multiplication, SODA 2017

title: Matching lower bound for OMv on low-VC-dimension matrices
W: Anand-van den Brand-McCarty give O~(n^2) preprocessing and O~(n^{2-1/d}) query time for Boolean Mv when M has VC-dimension d. Show, assuming OMv (or unconditionally in the cell-probe model), that n^{2-c/d} query time is necessary for some constant c, for d up to some omega(1) function; or improve the upper bound to n^{2-f(d)} with f(d) >> 1/d.
M: Lower bound: shows the OMv barrier degrades gracefully with structure, giving a quantitative 'OMv for structured inputs' hypothesis. Better upper bound: OMv hardness requires VC-dimension growing faster than believed, which would localize the hard instances.
why: This is the cleanest known structural parameter under which OMv fails; the authors state no matching lower bound is known.
status_notes: OMv open in general; Anand-van den Brand-McCarty (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.21240) show OMv fails for constant (corrupted) VC-dimension and note they have no matching lower bounds.
refs: Anand, van den Brand, McCarty, The Structural Complexity of Matrix-Vector Multiplication, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.21240
Henzinger, Krinninger, Nanongkai, Saranurak, Unifying and strengthening hardness for dynamic problems via the OMv conjecture, STOC 2015

title: Combinatorial BMM beating the sqrt(log n) saving
W: Give a combinatorial (no fast matrix multiplication) algorithm for n x n Boolean matrix multiplication or triangle detection in n^3/2^{omega(sqrt(log n))} time, e.g. n^3/2^{Omega(log^{0.6} n)}; or show the Cui-Liu-Woodruff decomposition (2^{O(d^2)} pieces) is optimal within the regularity/decomposition framework of Abboud et al.
M: Yes: first combinatorial saving exceeding the 2^{sqrt log n} saving of Williams' (non-combinatorial) APSP algorithm, and a step toward n^{3-eps}. Barrier: shows a quantitative limit of the 'structure vs randomness' approach to combinatorial BMM.
why: 2^{sqrt log n} is a recurring barrier (Williams APSP, Larsen-Williams OMv); combinatorial BMM just reached it in Nov 2026.
status_notes: AFKLM (STOC 2024) n^3/2^{Omega(log^{1/7} n)}; Cui-Liu-Woodruff (arXiv:2611.06717, Nov 2026, Lean-checked main theorem) reach n^3/2^{Omega(sqrt log n)} and note the combinatorial BMM hypothesis (no n^{3-eta}) is still consistent. AVW's APSP algorithm is non-combinatorial.
refs: Cui, Liu, Woodruff, Combinatorial Boolean Matrix Multiplication in n^3/2^{Omega(sqrt log n)} Time, arXiv:2611.06717
Abboud, Fischer, Kelley, Lovett, Meka, New graph decompositions and combinatorial Boolean matrix multiplication algorithms, STOC 2024
Alman, Vassilevska Williams, Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs, arXiv:2610.06783 (Oct 2026)

assumption: SETH / Orthogonal Vectors / Set Cover Conjecture
title: How fast does eps_k vanish for k-OV in low dimension?
W: Dürr-Kipouridis-Lampis-Węgrzycki show k-OV is solvable in O(2^{(1-eps_k)d} n) for every fixed k, and that eps_k -> 0 is forced by the Set Cover Conjecture. Determine the decay rate: prove eps_k >= c/log k (or c/k), or show that eps_k >= omega(1/k) would refute the Set Cover Conjecture.
M: A lower bound on eps_k is a quantitative near-refutation tool for SCC; an SCC-based upper bound turns SCC into a precise fine-grained statement about k-OV, sharpening the Björklund-Kaski link between SCC and the asymptotic rank conjecture.
why: It is one parameter, directly sandwiched between two famous conjectures (SCC and ARC), and the answer is unknown in either direction.
status_notes: SETH and OV are explicitly untouched by AVW (Oct 2026). Björklund-Kaski (STOC 2024) show ARC and SCC are not both true. ICALP 2026 (Dürr et al.) gives 2-OV in O(1.16^d n) and k-OV in 2^{(1-eps_k)d} n; under ARC a uniform eps exists.
refs: Dürr, Kipouridis, Lampis, Węgrzycki, Faster algorithms for k-Orthogonal Vectors in low dimension, ICALP 2026, arXiv:2507.11098
Björklund, Kaski, The Asymptotic Rank Conjecture and the Set Cover Conjecture are not both true, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.11926

title: Densest k-Subgraph and k-Biclique FPT-inapproximability from plain ETH
W: Prove, assuming only ETH, that Densest k-Subgraph cannot be approximated within k^{o(1)} (or any omega(1) factor) in f(k) n^{o(k)} time, or that k-Biclique has no f(k)n^{o(sqrt k)}-type algorithm, matching known Gap-ETH-based results.
M: Yes: removes Gap-ETH from another flagship parameterized-inapproximability result, continuing the PIH-under-ETH program. A barrier (e.g. showing DkS hardness needs average-case-type gap structure) would identify what Gap-ETH genuinely adds over ETH.
why: After Guruswami-Lin-Ren-Sun-Wu (PIH under ETH) and lattice results moving from Gap-ETH to ETH, DkS/k-Biclique are the prominent results still listed only under Gap-ETH.
status_notes: Gap-ETH remains unproven from ETH. PIH proved under ETH (Guruswami-Lin-Ren-Sun-Wu, STOC 2024); CVP_p and SVP_p (p>2) moved to ETH (Aggarwal-Gupta-Morolia-Zhang, ICALP 2026), which still list DkS/k-Biclique as Gap-ETH-only.
refs: Guruswami, Lin, Ren, Sun, Wu, Parameterized Inapproximability Hypothesis under ETH, STOC 2024, arXiv:2311.16587
Aggarwal, Gupta, Morolia, Zhang, Mind the Gap? Not for SVP Hardness under ETH!, ICALP 2026, arXiv:2504.02695
Chalermsook et al., From Gap-ETH to FPT-inapproximability, FOCS 2017

title: 2^{Omega(n)} hardness of Euclidean SVP under ETH
W: Show that approximate SVP in the l_2 norm (some constant gamma>1) has no 2^{o(n)}-time algorithm unless (randomized) ETH fails; or identify an obstruction (e.g. for the Z^n-based gadget) showing the l_p, p>2 technique cannot reach p=2.
M: Yes: grounds the concrete security of lattice cryptography (l_2 SVP) on ETH rather than Gap-ETH. Obstruction: explains why l_2 is special, complementing known barriers for SETH-hardness of CVP in even norms.
why: Stated as Open Problem 1 (p in [1,2], specifically p=2) in the ICALP 2026 paper; the most cryptographically relevant case.
status_notes: Aggarwal-Gupta-Morolia-Zhang (ICALP 2026) prove ETH-hardness for CVP_p (all p>=1) and SVP_p (p>2); p in [1,2] incl. p=2 left open. Earlier SVP_2 2^{Omega(n)} hardness required Gap-ETH-type assumptions.
refs: Aggarwal, Gupta, Morolia, Zhang, Mind the Gap? Not for SVP Hardness under ETH!, ICALP 2026, arXiv:2504.02695
Aggarwal, Stephens-Davidowitz, (Gap-)ETH-hardness of SVP, STOC 2018

assumption: Unique Games Conjecture / Small-Set Expansion Hypothesis
title: A super-constant-degree SoS integrality gap for Unique Games
W: Construct Unique Games instances with value <= eps on which degree-d Sum-of-Squares has value >= 1-eps, for some d = omega(1) (any slowly growing function of n), or show degree-O(1) SoS achieves a (1-eps, delta) distinguishing guarantee on all UG instances.
M: Gap: the first evidence that the strongest known algorithmic hierarchy fails on UG, strongly supporting UGC. Algorithm: refutes UGC (assuming NP is not in quasi-poly time for the 2-to-2 case), a major event.
why: Known gap instances (short code, noisy hypercube) are solved by constant-degree SoS (Barak et al. 2012), so the canonical lower-bound evidence for UGC is missing; this is the sharpest SoS-side test of the conjecture.
status_notes: UGC open; 2-to-2 Games theorem proved (Khot-Minzer-Safra 2018). Subexponential algorithm 2^{n^{poly(eps)}} (Arora-Barak-Steurer). To our knowledge no omega(1)-degree SoS integrality gap for UG is known (listed in Barak's SoS open problems). Not verified for 2025-26 developments.
refs: Barak, Brandão, Harrow, Kelner, Steurer, Zhou, Hypercontractivity, sum-of-squares proofs, and their applications, STOC 2012, arXiv:1205.4484
Khot, Minzer, Safra, Pseudorandom sets in Grassmann graph have near-perfect expansion, FOCS 2018
Barak, Sum of Squares: open problems (lecture notes)

title: Does UGC imply SSEH?
W: Give a polynomial-time reduction from Small-Set Expansion to Unique Games' hardness direction, i.e. prove UGC => SSEH (Raghavendra-Steurer proved SSEH => UGC), or exhibit an oracle/algorithmic separation (e.g. an algorithm for SSE on a class of graphs where UG remains as hard as in general).
M: Equivalence: UGC and SSEH merge into one hypothesis, so SSEH-based results (e.g. hardness of vertex expansion, balanced separator) inherit UGC's support. Separation: SSEH is strictly stronger, and should be regarded as the riskier assumption.
why: A standing structural question; many hardness results use SSEH instead of UGC with no justification that it is not stronger.
status_notes: Raghavendra-Steurer (STOC 2010) SSEH => UGC; converse open. UG on certified small-set expanders is easy (Bafna-Barak-Kothari-Schramm-Steurer, STOC 2021), consistent with SSE being the 'hard core'. No 2024-26 resolution found.
refs: Raghavendra, Steurer, Graph expansion and the Unique Games Conjecture, STOC 2010
Raghavendra, Steurer, Tulsiani, Reductions between expansion problems, CCC 2012, arXiv:1011.2586
Bafna, Barak, Kothari, Schramm, Steurer, Playing Unique Games on certified small-set expanders, STOC 2021, arXiv:2006.09969

title: A uniformly samplable counterexample to the poly-time low-degree conjecture
W: Mao's counterexample (permutation-invariant graph distributions with zero low-degree advantage up to degree Theta(log^{r-1} n) that a linear-time rank test detects after constant-rate resampling) needs non-uniform advice for its Reed-Muller subspace / evaluation-point seed. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs a good seed, giving a uniformly poly-time samplable counterexample; or show that every uniformly samplable permutation-invariant distribution with vanishing degree-polylog advantage is hard for poly-time noise-robust tests (a repaired conjecture).
M: Uniform counterexample: the low-degree heuristic is refuted even in its most cryptographically natural form, undermining low-degree-based hardness predictions (planted clique variants, tensor PCA, random CSPs). Repaired conjecture: gives the field a defensible replacement.
why: Stated open by Mao (Jul 2026); it is the single remaining gap between the polynomial-time counterexample and a fully satisfying refutation.
status_notes: Buhai-Hsieh-Jain-Kothari (arXiv:2505.17360, 2025) refuted the quasi-polynomial low-degree conjecture; Mao (arXiv:2607.20318, Jul 2026) refuted the polynomial-time graph version, leaving uniform samplability and a natural repair open. Planted clique itself (k = n^{1/2-delta}) remains believed hard.
refs: Mao, The Polynomial-Time Low-Degree Conjecture is False, arXiv:2607.20318
Buhai, Hsieh, Jain, Kothari, The Quasi-Polynomial Low-Degree Conjecture is False, arXiv:2505.17360
Hopkins, Statistical inference and the sum of squares method, PhD thesis 2018

title: Densest k-Subgraph approximation ratio implied by Feige's hypothesis
W: Feige (2002) showed his random 3-SAT hypothesis implies a constant-factor inapproximability for Densest k-Subgraph (and others). Prove that the hypothesis (possibly in its random 4-SAT/k-SAT form) implies DkS hardness within a factor growing with n (e.g. polylog n), or show a natural barrier: e.g. that any such reduction would also refute polynomial-time refutation algorithms at density n^{0.5}.
M: Yes: places superconstant DkS hardness on a worst-case-free, average-case assumption distinct from planted dense subgraph conjectures. Barrier: clarifies how much hardness random-CSP refutation assumptions can transfer.
why: Feige's hypothesis is the original average-case-to-approximation bridge; its strength relative to newer planted assumptions is poorly understood. Status of this exact target uncertain to us; graded C.
status_notes: Feige's hypothesis (constant clause density) is not threatened: poly-time refutation needs ~n^{1.5} clauses, matched by SoS lower bounds; Guruswami-Kothari-Manohar (STOC 2022) proved Feige's hypergraph Moore bound conjecture and semirandom refutation at the threshold. Exact openness of the DkS target not verified.
refs: Feige, Relations between average case complexity and approximation complexity, STOC 2002
Guruswami, Kothari, Manohar, Algorithms and certificates for Boolean CSP refutation: smoothed is no harder than random, STOC 2022, arXiv:2109.04415

title: Binary-error LWE with linearly many samples
W: For LWE with secret in Z_q^n (q = poly(n)) and errors uniform in {0,1}, given m = C*n samples for a fixed constant C > 1, either give a polynomial-time (or 2^{o(n)}) algorithm, or prove hardness from standard LWE/worst-case lattice problems for m = C*n (beyond the n(1+O(1/log n)) samples of Micciancio-Peikert).
M: Algorithm: rules out compact binary-error LWE parameter choices used in efficient schemes. Hardness: closes a decade-old gap between Arora-Ge linearization (m ~ n^2) and the known reduction, strengthening the LWE assumption family.
why: A precise, long-standing gap in a cryptographic assumption with practical consequences; neither direction is known.
status_notes: LWE remains unbroken classically and quantumly: Chen's 2024 quantum LWE algorithm was found to have a bug and withdrawn. Binary-error LWE: hard for m <= n(1+O(1/log n)) (Micciancio-Peikert 2013), poly-time via Arora-Ge for m = O(n^2); algebraic attacks give subexponential time with intermediate m. Regime m = Cn open.
refs: Micciancio, Peikert, Hardness of SIS and LWE with small parameters, CRYPTO 2013
Arora, Ge, New algorithms for learning in presence of errors, ICALP 2011
Albrecht, Cid, Faugère, Fitzpatrick, Perret, Algebraic algorithms for LWE problems, ACM CCA 2015
Aaronson, That IACR preprint (blog post on Chen 2024), scottaaronson.blog/?p=7946

assumption: Sparse LPN (k-sparse LPN, used for PRGs / iO)
title: Sparse 3-LPN at noise n^{-1/2}: beating Gaussian elimination
W: For 3-sparse LPN with m = n^{1.4} samples and noise rate eta = n^{-0.6} (or any eta in [n^{-0.7}, n^{-0.5}]), give an algorithm running in time exp(o(eta*n)), or prove a lower bound (e.g. for low-degree/SoS or statistical-query-like models) showing exp(Omega(eta*n)) is needed in this regime.
M: Algorithm: weakens the low-noise sparse LPN regimes assumed in some iO and PCG constructions. Lower bound: provides first evidence that the Chen-Shu-Zhou improvement threshold (eta < n^{-0.7}) is real.
why: Concrete parameter window just beyond the 2024-25 algorithmic frontier, directly relevant to sparse-LPN-based cryptography.
status_notes: Chen-Shu-Zhou (arXiv:2407.19215, COLT 2025) solve sparse LPN in e^{O(eta n^{(delta+1)/2})} with m ~ n^{1+(1-delta)(k-1)/2}; for k=3, m=n^{1.4} they beat e^{eta n} only for eta < n^{-0.7}. Constant-noise sparse LPN remains unbroken.
refs: Chen, Shu, Zhou, Algorithms for Sparse LPN and LSPN Against Low-noise, COLT 2025, arXiv:2407.19215
Applebaum, Exponentially-hard Gap-CSP and local PRG via local hardcore functions, FOCS 2017

assumption: Circuit lower bounds underlying derandomization (E needs exponential circuits)
title: From S_2E to E^NP: near-maximum circuit lower bounds
W: Prove E^NP is not contained in SIZE[2^n/n] (or even SIZE[2^{epsilon n}] for some eps>0 infinitely often); equivalently, put Range Avoidance in FP^NP for the relevant circuit classes, improving Li's FS_2^P algorithm.
M: Yes: an unconditional exponential lower bound one level lower than currently known, strengthening hardness-vs-randomness inputs (e.g. derandomization of AM / prBPP in P^NP-type classes). Barrier/relativization result: shows the symmetric-alternation step of Chen-Hirahara-Ren/Li is essential.
why: The 2023-24 breakthrough reached S_2E; E^NP is the natural next class and is explicitly the target of the range-avoidance program.
status_notes: Chen-Hirahara-Ren (STOC 2024) and Li (STOC 2024) proved S_2E needs 2^n/n circuits via FS_2^P range avoidance; Hitchcock (arXiv:2605.03306, 2026) shows such languages are comeager in S_2E. E^NP case remains open; BPP=P still conditional.
refs: Chen, Hirahara, Ren, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size, STOC 2024, arXiv:2309.12912
Li, Symmetric exponential time requires near-maximum circuit size: simplified, truly uniform, STOC 2024, arXiv:2310.17762
Hitchcock, Exponential-size circuit complexity is comeager in symmetric exponential time, arXiv:2605.03306

title: Breaking the log k barrier for 3-petal sunflowers
W: Show every family of more than (o(log k))^k sets of size k (e.g. (log k)^{(1-c)k} or (log log k)^{O(k)}) contains a sunflower with 3 petals.
M: Yes: first bound beyond what robust sunflowers can give (they provably need a log k factor), so a genuinely new non-robust technique, with applications to monotone circuit lower bounds and data structures. Failure of natural approaches clarifies whether C^k is plausible.
why: The robust-sunflower method is provably stuck at (O(w log k))^k; w=3 is the smallest open case of the Erdős-Rado conjecture and the most-studied.
status_notes: Best bound O(w log k)^k (Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2020; Rao; Bell-Chueluecha-Warnke), with a matching Omega(log k)^{k-sqrt k} lower bound for robust sunflowers; a 2025 survey (arXiv:2509.14790) states the conjecture open. A 2026 claim for shifted families (arXiv:2606.02667) appears to have a gap and does not cover general families.
refs: Alweiss, Lovett, Wu, Zhang, Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma, Annals of Math 2021
The Story of Sunflowers (survey), arXiv:2509.14790
Bell, Chueluecha, Warnke, Note on sunflowers, Discrete Math 2021
